title: Gold Falls Over 1% After U.S. PCE Inflation Data Comes in Line With Expectations
excerpt: Spot gold drops to $4,594 per ounce as the Fed's preferred inflation gauge shows 3.7% annual rise, keeping rate hike prospects alive.
body:
• Spot gold fell 1.3% to $4,594.84 per ounce after the U.S. PCE Price Index showed 3.7% annual inflation in July, largely in line with expectations.
  • Traders now price a 38% chance of a Fed rate hike in September, up marginally from 36% before the data release.
  • Gold had climbed to its highest level since May 14 on Tuesday before Wednesday’s pullback; analysts still see potential above $5,000 this year.

Gold prices extended their retreat on Wednesday after the U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index — the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation measure — came in largely as expected, reinforcing the prospect of tighter monetary policy and triggering profit-taking after a multi-week rally.

Spot gold fell 1.3% to $4,594.84 per ounce by late morning Eastern time, pulling back from the three-month high reached the previous session. U.S. gold futures dropped 0.9% to $4,650.90. The dollar strengthened 0.3%, adding pressure on bullion priced in the U.S. currency.

PCE Data and Fed Implications

The Commerce Department reported that the PCE Price Index rose 3.7% in the 12 months through July, slightly above the 3.6% consensus forecast from economists polled by Reuters. The reading leaves the Fed well above its 2% inflation target, maintaining pressure on policymakers weighing whether to raise rates further.

Markets reacted by marginally increasing the probability of a September rate hike to 38%, from 36% before the data, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. A 62% majority of traders still expect the Fed to hold rates steady next month.

“Gold’s price action up to today’s data was just some profit taking. PCE data came in largely in line with expectations, so we’re consolidating within yesterday’s range.”

— Peter Grant, Vice President and Senior Metals Strategist, Zaner Metals

Rally Context

The pullback follows a sharp rally that carried gold up roughly 15% over the past month, driven by Chinese and retail buying, a weaker dollar after the U.S. Treasury Department doubled the size of its longer-dated bond buyback operations, and persistent geopolitical risk from the Iran conflict.

Gold had surged to $4,696 on Tuesday, testing resistance near the $4,700 level. The three-month high attracted profit-taking even before the PCE release, with Comex gold settling 0.86% lower at $4,598.20 — the largest one-day decline since August 18.

Outlook

Despite Wednesday’s drop, the medium-term outlook remains constructive. Analysts point to several tailwinds: elevated U.S. debt levels, Chinese central bank buying, and geopolitical uncertainty from the Strait of Hormuz standoff.

“I think the uptrend in gold is beginning to reassert itself. So I do see potential back above $5,000 this year,” Grant said, adding that new all-time highs are possible by the second quarter of 2027.

Morgan Stanley analysts echoed the view, writing that with the Fed expected to hold rates, “we see scope for gold to exceed $5,000/oz in 2027, potentially earlier.”

Market attention now shifts to Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh’s remarks at the Jackson Hole symposium on Friday, which will provide further clues on the central bank’s policy trajectory. Gold has lost 13.5% from its January 2026 record of $5,318.40 but remains up 35% from its year-ago levels.
nri_angle: Gold remains a favored asset among Indian-American investors, and U.S. inflation and Fed policy directly affect both dollar-denominated gold prices and remittance economics.
